title: Grilled Shrimp Skewers with Mint Salsa Verde

ingredients.name: large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tail-on

steps: In a shallow dish, whisk together half of the lemon juice, 1 teaspoon olive oil, and minced garlic. Toss shrimp to coat, cover, and chill for 10 minutes.
In a small food processor, pulse green onions, mint, cilantro, capers, jalapeño, yogurt, water, salt, pepper, remaining lemon juice, and remaining olive oil until creamy.
Preheat a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and coat lightly with oil.
Remove shrimp from marinade, discarding residual liquid. Grill shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and pearly opaque throughout.
Drizzle the zesty herb salsa verde over the warm grilled shrimp and serve.
swaps: Greek yogurt can be replaced with sour cream or mayonnaise; jalapeño can be omitted for zero heat.
notes: Classic heart-healthy preparation. Grilling takes only 5 to 6 minutes total.

title: Shrimp Sauté with Garlic, Tomato, and Linguini

ingredients.name: medium-to-large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook linguini until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup pasta cooking water and drain.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink; transfer shrimp to a clean plate.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to pan drippings and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes until softened and juicy.
Return cooked shrimp and drained linguini to the skillet, tossing with reserved pasta water and chopped parsley to coat evenly.
Serve warm topped with freshly grated parmesan cheese.
swaps: Gluten-free pasta or zucchini noodles can substitute for linguini; canned diced tomatoes can replace fresh.
notes: Fast 25-minute weeknight dinner with rich tomato-garlic pan emulsion.

title: Quick Weeknight Shrimp Tacos with Slaw

source.name: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health

ingredients.name: raw shrimp, peeled, deveined, and tails removed
shredded red and green cabbage slaw

steps: In a medium bowl, toss peeled shrimp with olive oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add shrimp in a single layer and sear for 2 minutes per side until opaque and lightly spiced.
In a separate bowl, toss shredded cabbage with fresh lime juice, a drizzle of oil, and cilantro.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over an open flame for 30 seconds per side.
Assemble tacos by layering seasoned shrimp into warm tortillas, topping with cabbage slaw and fresh avocado slices.
swaps: Can use store-bought taco seasoning blend; Greek yogurt crema can be drizzled over top.
notes: Superfast 20-minute dinner; avoid overcooking shrimp so tacos remain tender and juicy.

title: Quick Shrimp and Veggie Sauté Lo Mein

source.name: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health

ingredients.name: lo mein egg noodles or ramen noodles
toasted sesame oil or peanut oil

steps: Cook noodles according to package instructions until tender; drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat 1 tablespoon sesame oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add shrimp and stir-fry for 2 minutes until pink; remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil to wok with minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss in sliced bell pepper, snap peas, and carrots, stir-frying over high heat for 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Whisk together soy sauce and oyster sauce. Add cooked noodles, sautéed shrimp, and sauce mixture to wok, tossing vigorously for 1 to 2 minutes until hot and coated.
swaps: Can substitute spaghetti or udon for lo mein noodles; tamari for gluten-free.
notes: One-pan noodle dinner packed with crisp vegetables and savory umami glaze.

title: Thai Red Curry Shrimp with Vegetables

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

ingredients.name: red bell pepper, sliced into strips

steps: Heat coconut oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add red curry paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and stir until the curry paste completely dissolves; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add sliced bell pepper and zucchini, simmering for 4 to 5 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Add raw shrimp and fish sauce to the simmering curry; cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes until shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Remove from heat, stir in fresh lime juice and Thai basil leaves, and ladle over steamed jasmine rice.
swaps: Can substitute green curry paste; sweet Italian basil works if Thai basil is unavailable.
notes: Adding shrimp at the final stage keeps them exceptionally tender and prevents curdling.

title: Traditional Shrimp & Chicken Okra Gumbo

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown diced chicken for 5 minutes, then remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil to pot and sauté onion, bell pepper, and celery (the Cajun holy trinity) for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, Cajun seasoning, sliced okra, diced tomatoes, and chicken broth, stirring well and bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, return chicken to pot, cover, and simmer gently for 25 minutes to blend flavors and allow okra to naturally thicken the broth.
Stir in raw shrimp and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Ladle hearty gumbo into bowls over scoops of warm white rice.
swaps: Can add andouille sausage for deeper smoke; frozen okra works just as well as fresh.
notes: Okra acts as a natural thickener; adding shrimp at the very end guarantees optimal texture.

title: Garlic Butter Shrimp Scampi

source.name: 45 Healthy Comfort Food Recipes - Food Network & Swanky Recipes

ingredients.name: large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tail-on

steps: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; drain and set aside.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter over medium-high heat.
Add shrimp in a single uncrowded layer and sear for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pink; remove to a warm plate.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to pan drippings, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in white wine and lemon juice, bringing to a simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Whisk in remaining 2 tablespoons cold butter and chopped parsley until a glossy emulsion forms.
Toss pasta and shrimp back into the skillet for 1 minute until warmed through and coated in glossy scampi sauce.
swaps: Chicken broth with 1 tsp lemon juice can substitute for white wine; serve with crusty bread instead of pasta.
notes: Classic Italian-American scampi. Swirling in cold butter off heat creates the silky restaurant emulsion.
